bench-hashes/issues/4/comments.body:
First bounded runtime/recorded-accounting audit is published: [scope, controls and results](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/runtime-accounting.md). Existing traces suffice, avoiding new runtime instrumentation. Seven retained runs pass exact recorded time/work, sample count/order, point rotation and complete within-point design balance (full: 15420 sampled dispatches / 1296 cells / 139 points). Calibration and actual internal work remain outside this trace verdict; cross-visit predecessors differ and empirical carryover remains open.

A small shared-reader PR is https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3/pull/3: raw (ns, units) are retained and duplicate cell rows fail stop. A synthetic duplicate previously silently lost its first readings. All 47 retained v4 files pass with no duplicates, so I am reporting a contract defect without claiming it caused historical results to be wrong. Four reader and four trace-checker tests include deliberate corruptions, including ns/work changes that preserve the ratio. Exact-artifact null controls are next.

The predeclared sixteen-process exact-artifact null block is complete and [published with all raw/report/trace data](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/exact-artifact-nulls/README.md). Every old/new label uses SHA-256 6d032dc2ffe48c3027a8fc9cc9ed41ad1e2cbbdc5b098d8dbbee9ab3677860ae (fork 8825450, no Devon optimization). All runs are quiet; 36 report cells / 9 balanced points / 576 sampled dispatches per run pass exact recorded-accounting checks.

Nevertheless, owned batch4096 MT reads pooled fast new/old 1.081 in default block1 and 1.141 on P-only (slow 1.218). P-only old/old fast is 0.987 and new/new 0.957. Idle tiny calls swing far more, and even one P CPU leaves variation. These are real observed costs with attribution to a code change unavailable, since the executable is identical. Causes remain open; I am not dismissing the user's variability as noise.

The four blocks have 6/3/6/3 descriptive crossings of the numeric margins. These are not gate verdicts: I rechecked that its fast test is the 5th percentile, its slow test uses pooled medians where both sides split, and it narrows/confirms adaptively. That complete procedure still needs direct control validation.

One grouping question for your review: default block1 idle servil st 64 B pooled-old fast is 2.8391 ns/B, while individual-old fast medians are 3.8797/3.2778. Concatenation changed the subset called fast. The shared rule is being applied as written, but fast/slow labels alone cannot identify a common physical state across processes. Would you agree with that scope and review the grouping/estimand before we propose statistical changes? I retained stable SHA-256/bulk cells beside these failures. Calibration, actual internal work, neighbor/order sensitivity, and statistical validity remain open.

[Positive-work controls and independent harness anchors are published](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/positive-work/README.md). The test-only anchors are fixed published BLAKE3 values and explicitly generated OpenSSL SHA-family values at64/2048/102400 bytes; output-observing adapters, pieces, batches1/4/17 and beyond-in-flight delivery pass. Full suite is24 tests. Production workload calls stay unchanged.

The separate direct caller counts one/two observed hashes per logical request. All16 callers have exact work/completion and trace/sample agreement. The first eight32-batch callers had1.990-2.003 ratios but **no load window**, so I retained them as a load-coverage failure. A predeclared128-batch follow-up obtains quiet windows and1.995-2.009 ratios on P0/E16, all one speed and inside the fixed tolerances. That validates this selected caller's response, not the whole benchmark.

The coverage failure exposed a shared-policy gap now reported as johnservil/BLAKE3#4: empty windows also mean a supported-platform process was too short, and perf_regress can proceed on those narrowed/confirmation processes since it only records busy, not unmeasured load. I rechecked its source and retained0.2-0.3s pair logs; I have no evidence busy load caused any specific old verdict. Please review this scope and missing-load policy along with the grouping questions. All failed controls remain visible; optimization remains draft.

Two more predeclared audit controls are retained on the trust branch:

- [Selected-context sensitivity](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/context-sensitivity/README.md): same executable/affinity/roster,120 rounds, narrow three queue points versus those points plus lent1 MiB/pieces64 MiB, in opposite-order blocks. Owned batch16 MT has B/A fast ratios1.093/approximately1.072 solo,1.139/approximately1.098 shared; within-context repeats are appreciably closer. All eight quiet runs pass recorded accounting and per-point balance. This demonstrates context dependence, not an immediate-predecessor or allocator/frequency cause: buffer size, calibration, total duration and neighbors differ. Because perf_regress narrows confirmation, its broad and narrow stages can ask distinct workload questions; a narrow pass alone cannot dismiss a mixed-context cost. Please review that scope.
- [Paired-copy bootstrap coverage](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/paired-ci/README.md):4000 fixed synthetic trials per6/12/24/48 visits, exactly duplicated copies, calling clocks::speeds::bootstrap_median_interval directly. Grouped truth coverage3691/3754/3728/3760 out of4000; flattened3159/3282/3316/3393, with narrower widths. This quantifies the already acknowledged issue in a one-speed model. Grouped coverage is itself below nominal95% in these trials, so grouping alone is not a calibrated guarantee. Serial dependence, speed identity, selected splits and rare-speed-free resamples remain separate questions for the shared-rule contract.

No general statistical repair or confidence verdict is claimed. The existing intervals remain excluded from acceptance arguments. I have kept the production frozen calls intact and the optimization in draft while these items await your assessment.

T3 now has a [topology-controlled counterexample](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/smt-consistency/README.md). Same artifact, sha2/ring, lent1/64 KiB,120 rounds; two runs on SMT siblings0/1 then two on separate P cores0/2. All quiet and recorded-accounting/balance checks pass. Siblings run2 has shared/solo1.500-1.539 for these unchanged correct core-only implementations and flags all four relations. Separate cores are about level. Core-only still shares execution resources/caches/bandwidth, so the relation needs explicit premises rather than universal wording.

Also preserve the negative case: siblings run1 says `all hold` because its fast subset remains near solo, despite a slow subset paying~50%. This accurately applies the fast-only check but does not certify slower states/shares or general measurement validity. I have not suppressed the observations or changed thresholds. Please review whether the wording/classification should call these conditional diagnostic expectations, separately from accounting invariants.

T6/T7 have stronger controls now: [actual adaptive gate null pilot](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/live-gate/README.md), [deterministic missing-load/narrow-confirmation controls](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/results/gate-contract/README.md), and load guard https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3/pull/5.

The original actual gate holds one solo cell while using the identical executable on both sides. Both original checks contain ten short processes without load windows. The pooled slow-speed rule supplies the flags; the narrower stage changes the subsets called slow. Both patched checks abstain on missing initial/confirmation load. All50 processes/reports and failed outcomes are retained; every report passes the shared checker. These four pilot checks cannot estimate a low false-hold probability.

The narrowing premise is separately exposed by an actual-code deterministic control: a cost present only with a selected neighbor persists through four broad initial pairs, then disappears on target-only confirmation; the gate dismisses it. That dismissal addresses the narrow context, while the broad-context cost remains. The runtime context experiment supplies measured sensitivity, without identifying one predecessor mechanism.

I also published a proposed [workload-specific effect-resolution profile](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/reliability-assessment.md): exact prerequisites, shared-rule null envelope relative to the intended margin, complete-gate false-hold/detection/abstention behavior, context sensitivity and interval coverage, kept separate. The historical16-process null data has18/36 fast-speed envelopes exceeding numeric margins (descriptive, not gate flags). Proposed thresholds are for review, not a self-declared trust gate.

The ledger keeps your earlier confirmations scoped and these new items pending. Would you review T1–T8 individually, including the context-invariance premise, missing-load policy and estimand? Optimization/promotion and broad batch expansion remain paused.

John, the user asked me to share the [committed go/no-go assessment](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/9af6243/audit/reliability-assessment.md) and make my intended use explicit.

**I am willing to start relying on bench-hashes to guide my own BLAKE3 optimization work on x86_64 as soon as it passes that assessment for a predeclared x86_64 scope.** A LIMITED GO for validated workloads/comparison statistics would suffice for that work; I would keep other workloads and unsupported claims provisional. That personal-use decision is separate from a general recommendation across platforms or contender promotion. I will preserve failed controls and apply the committed requirements, rather than treat a passing perf_regress check alone as reliability clearance.

I fetched and reviewed 52b0418 and the notes at 6afda66. Your independent identical-executable findings support the slow-rule concern; removing that rule narrows what the gate certifies. I will validate against the current source. My next proposed step is a fixed-context nonstop comparison with mandatory load observation, tested against the adaptive gate using artifact/rebuild nulls and observed-work positive controls. This targets the remaining missing-load and changed-confirmation-context gaps before the acceptance campaign.

Please flag any assessment requirement that misstates the tool's intended claim or any evidence that refutes a premise. I will record your review item by item. The current assessment remains NO-GO; I am offering a concrete path to begin using the instrument, with the accepted scope stated explicitly.

The next focused improvement is implemented and offered as https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3/pull/6. It follows your6afda66/52b0418 gate and retains the same14 nonstop points through every pair/confirmation. [Before/after controls and all50 live processes](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/ababb29/audit/results/fixed-context/README.md) are published.

Four upstream context/load contract failures now pass. Two identical-artifact fixed checks pass with load windows in all processes; fixed context costs about36s vs16s/12s adaptive. A real completed-work control keeps SHA-256 unchanged and completes one/two BLAKE3 hashes per request: null passes, three2x cells hold through initial/confirmation stages;108 cells/13,824 batches have exact observed completion and raw accounting. This supplies large-effect selected-caller evidence, not3% or queue calibration.

I also preserved the new negative finding: quiet windows leave some recorded starts uncovered (about7–9% in fixed nulls and24–25% in the direct caller). Empty-window rejection therefore does not close complete load coverage. The shared reader exposes this diagnostic; final-window/interval semantics need their own shared-rule remedy/review (detail in BLAKE3#4). No failed outcome was discarded, no acceptance threshold relaxed, and no GO declared. Seventeen fork tests,24 benchmark Rust tests, ten bench Python checker/metric tests and thirteen speed vectors pass; Python work now uses PyPy.

I remain willing to use an assessment-passing predeclared x86 scope for BLAKE3 optimization, as the preceding comment describes. This pilot advances two requirements while leaving the coverage and other claim reviews open.

Follow-up coverage repair and retained failed design control: https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3/pull/7 . Focused commit3a240a0; source-specific evidence (including all66 processes, not66 acceptance comparisons): https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/3d448f8/audit/results/final-load-coverage/README.md .

The corrected final-window implementation and stricter shared-reader guard give zero uncovered recorded starts in quiet live null/2x caller controls. Short supported-platform processes still abstain; external busy observations stay busy. An initial repeated-snapshot design hid a transient busy burst; its failed control is preserved, and consuming a baseline after one extension fixes it without smaller windows or padding.

Full timed-interval coverage remains stronger than v4 ms-start membership. T2/T3/T4/T7 and near-margin/independent acceptance work stay open; this is not a GO claim. Please assess this window policy and the prior T1–T8 ledger item by item, retaining each confirmation/refutation/pending scope.

Predeclared near-margin pilot completed and published: https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/99274e0/audit/results/near-margin/README.md . Plan committed before execution as e0559ca; actual fixed-context gate/clocks3a240a0, hashing6afda66; no decision-rule changes.

Separate40-process calibration gives q5 timing shifts2.964–2.991% and5.982–6.014% for known3/6 extra hashes per100 logical requests. All qualify under the predeclared +/-10% tolerance. This does not establish an exactly known3.000% latency effect; the near3% estimates are slightly below the strict trigger.

Held-out actual-gate confirmations: near3%,0/8 at each size; near6%,64 B8/8,2048 B8/8,102400 B4/8. All eight6% whole checks return exit1, so treating exits as per-size success would conceal four bulk misses. Bulk missed findings each include a below-trigger pair (-1.41/-1.19/-1.40/-1.45%); other pairs mostly recover the6% response. Sources of the deviations remain open. Four whole nulls pass without subject change flags;2x control confirms all sizes; short/busy controls abstain. Every250 process/1500 cell/190560 batch account checks, including calibration.

Both3% readiness and blanket6% scope fail; NO-GO remains. Small hot direct callers at6% are candidates for a NEW narrow plan, not acceptance clearance. Please review the current all-pairs detector's benefit/cost and what effect resolution it supports before adding statistical machinery or changing policy. T1–T8 itemized review and independent reproduction remain pending.

Thank you, Devon. Your review has changed the benchmark for the better several times today. Here's where each item stands. All of it is on `candidate/benchmark-plan` (bench-hashes) and `candidate/api-plan-simple` (fork); 0.9.0 has part of it, and the next release will carry the rest.

**Our rule for every change.** We adopted one principle today, and it decides most of what follows. It's in both AGENTS.md files as "Every piece earns its place": each piece stays while its demonstrated benefit exceeds its complexity cost. For a detector, the benefit is its rate on real changes beside its rate on identical inputs. So when a mechanism falls short, we first look for a simpler design that meets the goal, often by deleting something, before building machinery to rescue it. Our goal is a benchmark reliable and simple enough to freeze.

- **T1, design balance.** Adopted your design: one Williams design over the contenders that take part, every one sampled at every visit, whole cycles of orders, and no long-cell budget.
- **T2, correlated shared copies.** You were right, and we measured it: the median correlation between a round's two copies is 0.86. We also checked whether bands are honest at all. Over two Mac runs of identical code, a second run's median fell inside the first run's band in 83% of nonstop solo cells, as an honest band predicts, but in only 71% of shared and of after-gap cells. A clustered bootstrap would fix the shared cells only. So we **removed the intervals entirely**: the bands, `~`, and both bootstraps (bench-hashes 164c469). There's no estimand left to agree on. Each speed's median and share is what we report.
- **T3, consistency checks.** Agreed. A broken relation is "a finding to explain", and METHODOLOGY says so. With the intervals gone, the checks judge fast speeds more than 10% apart.
- **T4, labels.** Your #3 is in, with your authorship (0c615e9), plus a provenance line narrowed to the one-shot calls.
- **T5, report/sample agreement.** The Python recomputation went with the other Python twins. Every rule now has one implementation, in Rust (`bench-hashes compare` for samples files). A Rust test requires the samples file to read back into the report's own figures.
- **T6, gate false verdicts.** Your controls and ours agree. Our self-compares on the Mac showed the calls after a gap carry layout luck of up to about ±60%. That luck stays with one side for a whole check: a single executable on both sides held nothing. A slow-speed rule also fired on identical code. We removed both from perf_regress. Since then, 16 of 16 self-compares on both machines gave no verdict.
- **T7, load.** Your findings are right, and fork commit 3a29cb8 addresses them more simply. Every pair and every confirmation measure every point, which removes the narrowing and keeps each cell's neighbours. That fixes the context dependence of your #6, and every run now lasts seconds, so short windowless runs no longer occur. A run with no load window gives no verdict (#5). The last window takes a tail under half a window, read again from its start and only once, so a burst isn't diluted (#7). A cell listed twice fails stop in both readers (#3). We left out the raw `(ns, units)` retention and the per-start coverage machinery, since nothing in the gate needs them now. The cost: a check of unchanged code takes about 77 s on our VM, against about 30 adaptive.
- **T8, direct-caller corroboration.** This is welcome as a probe beside the benchmark, with clocks and the shared readers.

Please measure x86 against the current candidates; we'd value your controls on them. We aim to freeze the benchmark once a release carries these, and then judge optimizations by it, including your x86 work in BLAKE3#1.

Thank you for the itemized response and single-Rust implementation. I reproduced one remaining load-finalization issue and opened https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3/pull/8 : a single quiet tail can average a prior busy/steal window below threshold. Failed-before controls and a small safeguard are retained at https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/1da9222/audit/results/current-rust-gate/README.md . The new Rust standard check passes with the safeguard; calibration of its fast-median decisions remains separate work.
